transcript.text: Bosch integrated dishwasher showing E:15 and the pump keeps running. Model SMV4HTX31E. I've turned it off and on, still there

The E:15 code on your Bosch dishwasher means the anti-flood (water-protection) system has been triggered. This happens when water collects in the base pan of the machine, causing the drain pump to run continuously as a safety measure. This is usually caused by a leak somewhere—either from the door seal, a spray arm deflecting water outwards, or an internal hose/pump seal leaking into the base tray. It can also be triggered if the inlet hose connection at the tap is dripping onto the floor. First, please check: is there any water visible on the floor around the dishwasher right now?
No water on the kitchen floor, none at all. I can see a little shine of water in the base tray through a gap by the plinth though.

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. Since there is no water on your kitchen floor, the leak is coming from inside the dishwasher and dripping into this tray. Please pull the dishwasher out carefully (turn off the water tap first), tilt it slightly backwards onto a towel, and place a shallow tray or thick towels under the front base pan to catch any dripping water. Then run a short drain cycle with the door open. Does the water in the base tray refill from an internal leak inside the machine, or does it stay dry?

I can't pull it out or tilt it, it's fully integrated under the worktop and the kitchen plinth is glued at the ends. I'd have to damage it to get it off. Is there anything else I can check from the front?

Since you can't move the dishwasher, we have a safety limitation: the E:15 code means water is sitting in the base pan (the anti-flood tray) at the bottom of the machine. This water usually comes from an internal leak—most commonly a failing seal on the drain pump or a leaking hose connection inside the sump area. Because that tray is inaccessible without pulling the unit out, you cannot safely empty it yourself. While you wait for help, please do these quick checks from the front to rule out simple external causes:
1. Open the door and check the rubber seal around the tub edge for splits or debris caught in it.
2. Make sure nothing is deflecting the spray arms so they fire water directly at the door gap. If those look fine, the leak is probably internal (pump/tub). As you cannot access the base pan to drain it and reset the system safely, I recommend calling an engineer who can remove the dishwasher, empty the tray, and replace the faulty seal or hose.
Door seal looks okay, no splits or debris that I can see. I'm not sure how to check the spray arms properly, so I can't tell you about those.

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. This triggers the E:15 safety lock, which keeps the pump running until the water is removed. Because you cannot safely pull out this integrated unit to access and empty that base tray yourself, this requires an engineer. They will need to remove the dishwasher, drain the protection tray, find the leak, and fix it (often replacing a seal or hose). Please call a qualified appliance repair service for this.
